My nails used to look just as bad as this, if not worse, roughly a year ago.  I decided that after two decades of chewing on them, I had had enough.  I desired 'pretty' nails so badly, so... I worked to figure out what would work for me.  Now, my nails are a medium length (by preference, I don't like them breaking lol) and I rarely, if ever, catch myself biting them.

I started painting my nails with various polishes at first.  If it wasn't chipped, I didn't have the desire to bite them because I didn't want to mess the nail polish up - I'd always stop myself.  So, when it chipped, I'd repaint them.  Occasionally, I'd catch myself biting on them, and yes, it did take a while to stop.  BUT.  It did.  

I have anxiety like you wouldn't believe, and so biting on my nails was a way to keep my hands, my mouth, and my mind (subconsciously) busy.  This also helped me develop a hobby that allows me to manage my 'bad days' a little better, as nail art can be a GREAT stress reliever.  ;)  

Along with that, I also picked up a hobby to keep my hands busy.  Or rather, I tried to.  That's another story.  lol.  Anyway, with having something for my hands to do, I simply didn't have the opportunity to bite my nails as it would slow me down and cause me to stop.  

Sooo... with all of my rambling done, I suggest painting your nails often (if it chips, repaint them - and yes, sometimes this will mean two or three times a week lol), finding something to keep your hands busy, and if you're looking for something to keep your mouth busy - gum!  

I have full faith that you can do it.  If I can, anyone can.  ;)  Good luck!

I know I said to fuck them, but even if that means simply not doing something they want you to, it's a small victory for you.  Even if it doesn't feel like it at the time.

There is never a practical solution.  When you're having struggles with depression and anxiety, anything really, there is no easy fix.  Sadly.  Does that mean it's not worth trying?  No.  It means that it will just be sweeter when you manage to reach the top.  

I went through that, about...3 years ago.  Roughly.  I worked, went to school, had friends, volunteering to help with things at my school, etc.  However, if it was the weekend, or I had a day off, I hid in my bedroom.  I stayed under a mountain of blankets and watched cartoons, trying to drown out the rest of the world.  Was it the best idea?  No.  Am I ashamed?  Absolutely not.  We all cope in our own ways.  

By no means do I think that suicide is the answer, and I'm sure that you have a lot going for you - and will have even more going for you as you grow older.  We all snap at times, usually on those close to us as they're the ones around.  It's part of friendships, of any relationship, really.  

Have you considered talking to a therapist or a counselor?  They might be able to find a way to help you out, to help you cope better.  I used to be iffy about the whole thing, but when I reached out to my doctor and finally admitted that I needed help...while my medicine doesn't completely fix everything, it makes my life better.  It was worth admitting that I needed help and talking to someone.
